title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients.

title: Risk factors associated with the development of a catheter-related thrombosis in patients with critical illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity.

SOURCES: We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach.

PRINCIPLE FINDINGS: We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%].

CONCLUSIONS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles.

title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.

RESULTS: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI).

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl2-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM.

title: Microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and endovascular treatment of sylvian fissure arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review.
abstract: Sylvian-fissure-region arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are uncommon and anatomically heterogeneous; published labels often describe non-comparable lesions or populations. To update evidence for microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), and endovascular treatment (EVT). Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched through May 2026 with citation chaining. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Dedicated sylvian/perisylvian cohorts were distinguished from broader cohorts and contextual technical reports. Incompatible endpoints, non-independent arms, and potentially overlapping cohorts were not pooled. Risk of bias and applicability were appraised. Nineteen reports were retained: 16 in the evidence synthesis and 3 as contextual background. Microsurgery achieved complete resection in 8/8, 40/41, and 94/94 patients. Transient deficits occurred in 4/8, 4/28, 9/94, and 18/41 patients; postoperative hematoma occurred in 2/94. Mortality windows varied. In the dedicated SRS cohort (n = 87), actuarial obliteration was 35% at 3 years, 60% at 4-5 years, and 76% at 10 years. Cumulative post-SRS hemorrhage was 5% at 1, 5, and 10 years (approximately 1% annually during latency); mortality was unreported. No dedicated curative EVT series for true sylvian AVMs was identified; available data described broader middle cerebral artery cohorts without sylvian-specific angiographic cure. Microsurgery is supported for carefully selected accessible sylvian-fissure AVMs, whereas SRS and embolization have complementary roles. Comparative superiority cannot be inferred. Future studies require explicit anatomical definitions, modality-specific denominators, angiographic endpoints, and standardized follow-up.

title: Incidence of Venous Thromboembolism After Elective Isolated Lumbar Decompression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched on March 2, 2026, with surveillance through June 17, 2026. Decompression-only cohorts without fusion or instrumentation were eligible. Clinically detected, coded, or patient-reported outcomes were analyzed separately by event type and follow-up using random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models when at least five studies contributed data. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies had a combined reported sample size of 831,732 patients. At 30 days, pooled DVT incidence was 0.283% (9 studies; 235,490 patients; 95% CI, 0.203%-0.393%) and PE incidence was 0.273% (7 studies; 235,341 patients; 95% CI, 0.171%-0.437%). At 90 days, DVT incidence was 0.225% (7 studies; 163,074 patients; 95% CI, 0.056%-0.905%) and PE incidence was 0.183% (6 studies; 162,772 patients; 95% CI, 0.041%-0.825%). Composite VTE estimates were heterogeneous. The low 30-day DVT and PE estimates persisted in leave-one-out analyses, while 90-day estimates were more sensitive to study inclusion. Only three studies reported chemical prophylaxis regimens. Different cohorts contributed to the two windows, which should not be interpreted as a temporal trend.

CONCLUSION: Reported 30-day DVT and PE incidences after isolated lumbar decompression were each approximately three events per 1,000 patients. These estimates provide a procedure-specific benchmark for counseling but do not establish the risk without prophylaxis or the effectiveness and overall benefit of chemoprophylaxis.
englishSummary: STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Tracheo-Innominate Artery Fistula for Severe Motor and Intellectual Disabilities.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracheo-innominate artery fistula (TIF) is a lethal post-tracheostomy complication. In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female with cerebral palsy developed massive tracheal hemorrhage 2 months post-tracheostomy. She presented with unstable vital signs, requiring manual syringe-push transfusion. Under cuff tamponade, emergency endovascular therapy (EVT) with Gore Viabahn and Viabahn VBX was chosen over open surgery due to thoracic deformities and limited time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) localized the angiographically occult rupture site. Hemostasis was achieved, but suspected stent graft infection developed on Day 11 despite prophylactic antibiotic therapy. Following transition to comfort care, she died 27 days post-procedure due to anemia, hypotension, and impaired ventilation.

CONCLUSION: Emergency IVUS-guided EVT under cuff tamponade is a valuable life-saving strategy and potential definitive treatment option for TIF in patients with prohibitive surgical risk, though late-onset infection remains a critical challenge.

In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis. title: Twenty-Year Forecast of Thoracic Surgeon Demand in Chile: Simulated Scenarios Using Bayesian Methods and Publicly Available Data.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years.

METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024). Surgeons practicing cardiac or vascular surgery, retirees, and those living abroad were excluded. A Bayesian projection model was developed that incorporates parameters such as retirement age, entry of new surgeons (including graduates and foreign-certified individuals), accidental mortality, population growth, and dynamic demand growth. Monte Carlo simulations (1000 iterations) were conducted across five scenarios (1 to 5 graduates/year, plus one certified surgeon/year). Absolute error analysis identified the optimal annual number of new graduates.

RESULTS: Of the 107 thoracic surgeons listed in Chile, only 67 were actively practicing non-cardiac thoracic surgery. The majority were concentrated in the Metropolitan Region (capital). Sex distribution was predominantly male (83.5%), with a mean age of 50.2 years. The corrected model (using 67 active surgeons as the baseline) shows that a scenario with 1 graduate per year results in a projected shortage, while scenarios with 3-5 graduates per year lead to potential oversupply. The optimal scenario, minimizing supply-demand mismatch, was training approximately two to three surgeons per year (2.6 graduates/year).

CONCLUSIONS: Strategic workforce planning is essential to avoid future imbalances in thoracic surgeon availability. Bayesian modeling provides a robust framework for anticipating demand, guiding training capacity, and ensuring equitable distribution across regions, thereby avoiding both shortages and saturation of the specialty in Chile.

There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years. METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024).

title: Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.

METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association.

CONCLUSION: Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs. METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026.

title: A Ten-Year Single-Center Evaluation of In-Hospital Versus Seven- Versus Thirty-Day Outcomes as Quality Standards After Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains a cornerstone for stroke prevention. The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine. This study evaluates institutional compliance with ESVS thresholds and compares the reliability of in-hospital and 7-day outcomes versus the 30-day follow-up interval.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted at the Medical University of Graz, encompassing 2496 patients undergoing primary CEA between 2014 and 2023. Data were retrieved from the institutional information system and cross-referenced with national mortality registries (Statistik Austria) to ensure comprehensive follow-up. Primary endpoints included stroke and death within 7 and 30 days, stratified by symptomatic status and surgical technique-Eversion Endarterectomy (EEA) versus Conventional Endarterectomy (TEA) with patch angioplasty.

RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 2496 eligible procedures. Notably, a substantial proportion of events that occurred after hospital discharge, accounting for 17.9% (10/56) of all 30-day strokes and 60.0% (9/15) of all 30-day deaths were observed between hospital discharge and postoperative day 30. Overall, the in-hospital combined stroke and death rate was 1.5% for asymptomatic patients and 3.8% for symptomatic patients. Following discharge, additional events were recorded in 10 asymptomatic and 9 symptomatic patients, resulting in a cumulative 30-day combined stroke and death rate of 2.0% [95% CI: 1.4%-2.7%] for asymptomatic patients and 5.3% [95% CI: 3.5%-7.2%] for symptomatic patients, thereby meeting ESVS safety standards. While symptomatic status was a significant predictor of complications (p < 0.001), neither sex nor surgical technique (EEA vs. TEA-patch) exerted a significant influence on outcomes.

CONCLUSION: CEA is performed at ESVS-recommended safety levels in Graz. Contrasting a clinical tendency to favor more convenient in-hospital metrics, this study demonstrates that "in-hospital" data cannot be standardized due to highly variable discharge windows. Furthermore, while fixed 7-day complication rates provide a standardized timeline, they still significantly underestimate perioperative risks. The substantial rate of post-discharge perioperative strokes and deaths observed in our cohort underscores the clinical necessity of extending quality control to at least 30 days, which remains the superior metric for clinical audit.

The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine.

title: Thromboembolic Complications in Cushing's syndrome: Origin, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cushing's syndrome (CS) is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which may persist after surgery and biochemical remission. This review synthesizes current evidence on VTE risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical assessment, and prevention and treatment strategies in patients with CS.

METHODS: This narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant English-language publications from 1999 through August 2026. Eligible sources included observational studies, case series, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical guidelines, and consensus statements addressing thrombotic risk, venous thromboembolism, or mechanisms of hypercoagulability in CS. Relevant findings were synthesized qualitatively and organized thematically.

RESULTS: A systematic meta-analysis reported approximately 18-fold higher odds of spontaneous VTE in patients with endogenous CS than in the general population. The prothrombotic state involves alterations in coagulation, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, platelet activation, inflammation, and venous stasis. Thrombotic risk may persist after biochemical remission, although its duration remains uncertain. The 2025 international Delphi consensus supports individualized thromboprophylaxis, with low-molecular-weight heparin preferred. Evidence supporting direct oral anticoagulants for prophylaxis remains limited. Clinical decisions should account for thrombotic and bleeding risks, including perioperative bleeding and potential drug interactions between direct oral anticoagulants and steroidogenesis inhibitors. No validated CS-specific risk prediction tool is available; a proposed framework may support individualized risk assessment. Proposed genetic, epigenetic, and non-coding RNA mechanisms remain hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSION: VTE prevention in CS requires individualized risk assessment and careful consideration of perioperative and post-remission risk. Prospective studies are needed to establish optimal prophylaxis strategies and validate CS-specific risk prediction approaches.

This review synthesizes current evidence on VTE risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical assessment, and prevention and treatment strategies in patients with CS. METHODS: This narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant English-language publications from 1999 through August 2026.

title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.

REVIEW METHODS: Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported.

RESULTS: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.

CONCLUSION: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.

title: Delayed Candida glabrata-associated infected thoracic aortic aneurysm after candidemia supported by identical serial MLVA profiles: a case report.
abstract: Candida-associated infected aortic aneurysms (AAs) are exceptionally rare and frequently fatal. A 76-year-old man developed Candida glabrata candidemia after surgery for ascending colon cancer; the postoperative course was complicated by an anastomotic leak and intra-abdominal infection. Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures. Approximately 1 year later, an enlarging descending thoracic AA was detected and treated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). Despite initially negative blood cultures, a normal or only minimally elevated serum β-D-glucan concentration, and negative Candida antigen testing, the aneurysm subsequently enlarged and required repeat TEVAR. Periaortic soft-tissue changes transiently regressed, further obscuring the diagnosis. Three months after the second TEVAR, computed tomography revealed renewed aneurysm enlargement and perigraft gas. C. glabrata was recovered from one of five blood culture sets. On the fifth day of admission, the patient experienced abrupt circulatory collapse with hemoptysis and died, likely due to aneurysm rupture through an aortobronchial fistula. All available intra-abdominal and bloodstream isolates of C. glabrata obtained throughout the clinical course had identical six-locus multiple-locus variable-number tandem-repeat analysis (MLVA) profiles. A prior episode of candidemia remains clinically relevant when a new or progressive aortic lesion develops, even after prolonged culture negativity. Serial aneurysm enlargement, periaortic inflammation, and delayed perigraft gas should outweigh apparently reassuring blood cultures or fungal biomarkers and should prompt early multidisciplinary reassessment, pursuit of tissue diagnosis when feasible, source control, and prolonged antifungal therapy.

Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures.

title: Trends and Impact of Early Medical Complications in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Data from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early medical complications following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are common and might increase poststroke morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to evaluate trends in the prevalence of early medical complications over almost 2 decades and their impact on 3-month functional outcome and mortality.

METHODS: A total of 181,704 AIS patients from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry (2006-2024) were analyzed. Early medical complications included decompensated heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia, sepsis, pneumonia, urinary tract infection (UTI), deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after 3 months, with favorable outcome defined as mRS ≤1. Associations between early medical complications and mRS were analyzed using multivariable Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: Among all patients, 16,279 (9.0%) had early medical complications. Pneumonia (4.2%), UTI (2.9%), cardiac arrhythmia (1.4%), and decompensated heart failure (1.4%) were most common, with significant declines in prevalence over time. Admission NIHSS scores decreased, and the use of intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy increased. Decompensated heart failure (RR = 1.85, 95% CI: 1.73-1.97, p < 0.001), sepsis (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.53-1.99, p < 0.001), pulmonary embolism (RR = 1.67, 95% CI: 1.33-2.10, p < 0.001), and pneumonia (RR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.57-1.72, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with 3-month mortality. Furthermore, the complications least associated with a favorable outcome were pneumonia (RR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.32-0.41, p < 0.001), decompensated heart failure (RR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.32-0.46, p < 0.001), and sepsis (RR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.45-0.77, p < 0.001). The effect sizes did not change significantly through the observed years.

CONCLUSIONS: This study observed a significant reduction in the prevalence of early medical complications after AIS, especially decompensated heart failure, pneumonia, sepsis, and pulmonary embolism which continue to substantially affect mortality and functional outcome in AIS patients.

This study aimed to evaluate trends in the prevalence of early medical complications over almost 2 decades and their impact on 3-month functional outcome and mortality. METHODS: A total of 181,704 AIS patients from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry (2006-2024) were analyzed.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

MAIN SYMPTOMS AND IMPORTANT CLINICAL FINDINGS: A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved.

MAIN DIAGNOSES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS, AND OUTCOMES: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.

Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

title: Limb Salvage and Clinical Outcomes of Percutaneous Versus Surgical Deep Venous Arterialization for No-option Chronic Limb-threatening Ischaemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare percutaneous with surgical deep venous arterialization for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia and to examine whether percutaneous outcomes differ by device type.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEDLINE was searched via PubMed on 8 August 2026. Eligible cohorts reported at least 10 limbs with Rutherford class 5 or 6 chronic limb-threatening ischaemia. Hybrid procedures were classified as surgical; superficial venous arterialization was excluded. The primary endpoint was 12-month limb salvage. Proportions were pooled on the logit scale using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals. Device type was a pre-specified secondary analysis.

RESULTS: Eleven cohorts comprising 470 limbs were included-eight percutaneous (382 limbs) and three surgical or hybrid (88 limbs). Pooled 12-month limb salvage was 71.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 66.0-75.5%; I2 = 0.5%), with no significant difference between modalities (71.8% vs. 72.6%; p = 0.81). Technical success was 95.9% (91.7-98.0%) and did not differ between modalities (p = 0.69), but within the percutaneous arm was higher with a dedicated system than with off-the-shelf technique (97.9% vs. 94.3%; p = 0.03). Amputation-free survival was 59.5% (50.1-68.2%), and reintervention occurred in 43.5%; neither was reported by any surgical cohort. Egger test indicated small-study effects (p = 0.009).

CONCLUSION: Deep venous arterialization achieved limb salvage in approximately 71% of patients with no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia. Limb salvage did not differ between percutaneous and surgical approaches, whereas technical success was higher with a dedicated device. These indirect comparisons from single-arm cohorts do not establish superiority of either technique.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3 a-Systematic review of non-randomized observational studies.

title: Low-Dose Versus High-Dose Drug-Coated Balloon After Jetstream Atherectomy for Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Lesions: The JUPITER Multicenter Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Second-generation low-dose drug-coated balloons (LD-DCBs) have shown clinical efficacy comparable to high-dose DCBs (HD-DCBs) for femoropopliteal artery (FPA) lesions. Whether paclitaxel dose density remains clinically relevant after aggressive vessel preparation with atherectomy in severely calcified FPA lesions remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

AIMS: This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 262 patients with severely calcified FPA lesions who underwent endovascular therapy with Jetstream atherectomy followed by second-generation LD-DCB (n = 175) or HD-DCB (n = 87). Propensity-score matching yielded 79 well-balanced pairs. The primary outcome was 1-year primary patency; secondary outcomes included freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization (TLR), limb salvage, and overall survival.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort before matching, 1-year primary patency was similar between second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB (86.8% vs. 83.1%, log-rank p = 0.578), with comparable freedom from TLR, limb salvage, and overall survival. After propensity score matching, primary patency remained similar between groups (88.5% vs. 84.9%, log-rank p = 0.588), as did freedom from TLR, limb salvage, and overall survival. Findings were consistent across calcification-related subgroups. In an exploratory Cox analysis, second-generation LD-DCB was not associated with an increased risk of restenosis compared with HD-DCB.

CONCLUSIONS: After Jetstream atherectomy for severely calcified FPA lesions, second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB were associated with comparable 1-year clinical outcomes, suggesting that either strategy may be a reasonable treatment option.

Whether paclitaxel dose density remains clinically relevant after aggressive vessel preparation with atherectomy in severely calcified FPA lesions remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

title: Influence of pathologic fractures on oncologic outcomes in extremity Ewing sarcoma: a single-institution retrospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathologic fractures occur in 5%-10% of patients with Ewing sarcoma and may influence the local treatment strategies. However, their prognostic impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the clinical course of patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma and pathologic fractures using a propensity score-matched analysis.

METHODS: This retrospective single-institution study reviewed 149 patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma treated between 2003 and 2020, including 12 patients (8.1%) with pathologic fractures. For comparison with patients without pathologic fractures, a 1:3 propensity score-matched control group (n = 36, adjusted group) was constructed.

RESULTS: Among the 12 patients, limb-sparing surgery was performed in 11 patients (91.7%), and limb salvage was finally achieved in 10 patients (83.3%). Three-year overall survival was 75.0% in patients with pathologic fractures, and 78.8% (unadjusted, P = .62) and 82.0% (adjusted, P = .60) in patients without pathologic fractures. Local recurrence was observed in two patients (16.7%) in the pathologic fracture group; both had a poor histologic response.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, pathologic fractures were not associated with a statistically significant difference in oncological outcomes. Limb-sparing surgery may be considered in selected patients, particularly when preoperative treatment is effective. However, the small number of the patients with the fracture limits statistical power and generalizability of the results.

This study evaluated the clinical course of patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma and pathologic fractures using a propensity score-matched analysis.

title: Venous thromboembolism and transfusion outcomes following intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total hip arthroplasty: A prospective two-center cohort study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used during total hip arthroplasty (THA) to reduce perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements. Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

METHODS: This prospective, observational, descriptive, two-center cohort study included consecutive adults who underwent elective primary THA. Patients received intravenous TXA according to institutional protocols. The primary outcome was the occurrence of symptomatic VTE, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction during a 10-week follow-up period. The secondary outcomes included blood transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin levels, and emergency department visits.

RESULTS: A total of 151 primary THAs were performed in 133 patients. One case of symptomatic DVT was diagnosed, corresponding to a VTE incidence of 0.75%. Five patients (3.8%) required postoperative blood transfusions, including two complex reconstructive procedures. The mean postoperative hemoglobin level was 11.8 ± 1.9 g/dL. No pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction was observed during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective two-center cohort of patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary THA, including both conventional and complex cases, a low incidence of symptomatic VTE and transfusion was observed. These results provide prospective real-world evidence from a Latin American population and contribute to the regional literature on perioperative blood conservation strategies for primary THA.

Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

title: Cost-utility analysis of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease patients with posterior hemorrhage in Japan.
abstract:
AIMS: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease (MMD) patients with posterior hemorrhage from the perspective of the Japanese public healthcare payer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We developed a combined decision tree and Markov model for adult posterior hemorrhagic MMD patients (mean age: 41 years; baseline modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) over a 60-year lifetime horizon with 1-year cycles. We estimated the treatment effect using the composite endpoint hazard ratio (0.07) from the JAM Trial posterior hemorrhage subgroup as a proxy for the effect on recurrent hemorrhage. We informed health utilities with recent EQ-5D-5L data from the Fukuoka Stroke Registry, weighted by the Japan Stroke Data Bank. We estimated direct medical costs based on the national fee schedule. We discounted costs and outcomes at 2% annually. We set the willingness-to-pay threshold at JPY 7,500,000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY).

RESULTS: In the base case, surgical revascularization yielded 21.49 QALYs for JPY 6,323,426 (USD 40,302), compared with 15.59 QALYs and JPY 5,308,637 (USD 33,835) for conservative management. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was JPY 172,220 (USD 1,098) per QALY, which falls below the reference value of JPY 7,500,000 per QALY. In scenario analyses with 5- and 10-year horizons, the ICERs were JPY 8,926,784 and JPY 2,031,693 per QALY, respectively. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis also favored surgical revascularization across the modeled parameter distributions.

LIMITATIONS: The base-case estimate of surgical efficacy was based on a composite outcome from a small subgroup, and long-term recurrence risks beyond the 5-year trial period remain uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Surgical revascularization is likely to be cost-effective for adult MMD patients with posterior hemorrhage within the Japanese healthcare system, although limited evidence leaves uncertainty about long-term rebleeding risks and the durability of surgical benefit.

title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge.

RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke.

title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Description of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (DATE-PAD).
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe real-world antithrombotic prescribing patterns following endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD), and to compare short-term efficacy and safety outcomes between dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and single antiplatelet therapy plus oral anticoagulant (SAPT+OAC) regimens.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. Patients with surgical interventions for PAD during the same admission were excluded. Primary outcome was the frequency of DAPT compared to SAPT+OAC discharge regimens. Secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day readmissions, bleeding, ischemic events, and amputations all within 90 days.

RESULTS: Of 221 patients, 86% were discharged on DAPT and 14% on SAPT+OAC. Low dose aspirin and clopidogrel was the predominant DAPT regimen (94%). Apixaban was the most common anticoagulant (71%), with 75% of patients receiving 5 mg twice daily dosing. SAPT+OAC was more frequently used in ALI (50%) than CLTI (10%). No significant differences were observed in 30- or 90-day readmissions, bleeding rates, amputations, or ischemic events.

CONCLUSIONS: DAPT remains the predominant regimen post-revascularization despite recommendations for low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin. Apixaban was the predominant anticoagulant despite the paucity of data for use in this population. Comparable short-term outcomes suggest both DAPT and SAPT+OAC regimens may be viable, though further research is needed to clarify optimal anticoagulant of choice and dosing, particularly for apixaban.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net (2D and 3D), and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet (2D and 3D). We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetic Foot Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Perfusion Assessment, and Implications for Pre-Revascularization Evaluation.
abstract: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of ulceration, infection, lower-extremity amputation, and premature mortality. Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes. Its implications for interpreting perfusion tests, assessing prognosis, and evaluating patients before revascularization remain insufficiently integrated in the existing literature. This narrative review examines MAC as a distal arterial phenotype with diagnostic and prognostic relevance in diabetic foot disease. Targeted PubMed searches updated on 22 September 2026, supplemented by reference checking and topic-specific searches, informed a qualitative synthesis of clinical, imaging, and mechanistic studies. The review distinguishes medial from intimal calcification and evaluates recognition, scoring, and renal, metabolic, and neurovascular mechanisms. Observational cohorts of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) and chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) link higher calcification burden with delayed healing, amputation, incomplete haemodynamic improvement, and selected systemic outcomes, although adjustment and endpoint definitions vary. In the MAC-prone diabetic foot, reliance on the ankle-brachial index alone may be misleading because calcified tibial and pedal arteries can produce falsely normal or elevated ankle pressures. Toe pressure, toe-brachial index (TBI), transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2), skin perfusion pressure (SPP), anatomical imaging, and careful wound trajectory assessment should therefore be integrated with established limb-threat and anatomical classifications. Emerging evidence suggests that MAC scoring may complement Wound, Ischaemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) staging, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) assessment, and small artery disease scoring in estimating wound-healing probability and amputation risk before revascularization. MAC scoring remains an adjunctive risk marker rather than a validated determinant of revascularization modality or a proven therapeutic target. Prospective studies should determine whether adding MAC assessment to established clinical models improves management and patient outcomes.

Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes.

title: Comparative evaluation of handheld vs. high-end ultrasound systems for TIPSS hemodynamic assessment: first impressions.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time.

RESULTS: Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows.

CONCLUSION: Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: No clinical trial registration was performed, as this study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis based on existing clinical data. The study did not involve prospective patient enrollment, international procedures, or assignment to treatment groups. Therefore, registration in a clinical trial registry was not applicable.

Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled.

title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.

RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery.

title: Indirect versus combined bypass for perfusion-defined high-risk adult moyamoya disease: a propensity score overlap-weighted analysis of revascularization and postoperative stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024. The cohort wasrestricted to hemispheres with a preoperative tissue volume of at least 59.5 mL showing time-to-maximum (Tmax) >6 seconds (6s). Revascularization was assessed by 6-month angiography using the Matsushima grading system, and perfusion improvement was evaluated using postoperative CT perfusion. Baseline imbalance was addressed using overlap-weighted propensity score analysis. Factors associated with postoperative stroke were evaluated using overlap-weighted logistic regression, with sensitivity analyses using patient-clustered robust standard errors and Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 124 hemispheres were analyzed (CB, 88; IB, 36). Before weighting, PCA involvement was more frequent in the IB group (86.1% vs. 61.4%; standardized mean difference = 0.586), but all prespecified covariates were balanced after overlap weighting. Good revascularization was comparable between CB and IB before weighting (93.2% vs. 94.4%, p = 1.000) and after overlap weighting (90.6% vs. 98.1%, p = 0.102). Postoperative perfusion outcomes were also similar. Postoperative stroke occurred less frequently after IB both before weighting (5.6% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.021) and after overlap weighting (5.2% vs. 34.6%, p < 0.001). In the overlap-weighted multivariable model, IB was associated with lower odds of postoperative stroke, whereas larger preoperative Tmax>6s volume was associated with higher odds. These findings remained significant after adjustment for intra-patient correlation and were directionally consistent in Firth analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort, IB achieved angiographic and perfusion outcomes comparable to CB, with a lower observed postoperative stroke. IB may be a reasonable risk-adapted option for selected high-risk hemispheres, although non-randomized treatment allocation warrants cautious interpretation.

We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated.

RESULTS: No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study.
