title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition.

RESULTS: Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.
englishSummary: AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers.

title: Nursing-Related Risk Characteristics and Identification of High-Risk Patients With In-Hospital Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract:
AIM: Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024. Of 783 patients screened, 71 were excluded, leaving 712 in the source cohort (61 DVT cases and 651 ultrasound-negative, matchable controls). Cases and controls were matched 1:3 without replacement by age (±5 years), sex, and fracture site, yielding 61 matched sets (244 patients). After matching, non-matching variables were singly imputed using a random forest algorithm for the primary analysis. To assess uncertainty associated with this approach, a separate sensitivity analysis generated 20 completed datasets from the pre-imputation matched records using a stochastic chained-equation multiple-imputation procedure. Regression estimates across the 20 datasets were combined using Rubin's rules. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Incremental within-set concordance was corrected using 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples. The primary analysis, complete-case analyses and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis were conducted separately.

RESULTS: Matching variables were well balanced after matching, with standardized mean differences (SMD) of 0.02 for age and 0 for sex and fracture site, although several non-matching characteristics remained imbalanced. Three factors were positively associated with in-hospital DVT: admission Caprini ≥9 (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.28-4.61), severe POD1 activity dependence (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.38-10.94), and preoperative immobilization ≥72 h (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.14-5.67). Compared with patients without any core risk features, the OR increased to 2.81 (95% CI 1.46-5.38) among those with one feature and to 6.28 (95% CI 1.57-25.03) among those with two features. Adding severe POD1 activity dependence to Caprini ≥9 was associated with a modest increase in corrected within-set concordance from 0.589 to 0.633, corresponding to a difference of 0.044 (bootstrap SE 0.022, 95% CI 0.003-0.088). Sensitivity analyses generally preserved the direction of the main associations, although the Caprini estimate was attenuated after additional adjustment for trauma-related variables and D-dimer.

CONCLUSIONS: Admission Caprini ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h, and severe POD1 activity dependence were each associated with in-hospital lower-extremity DVT. POD1 activity assessment was associated with a modest improvement in within-set risk ranking beyond Caprini stratification. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; however, it may help guide nursing attention toward prophylaxis delivery, activity support, and symptom surveillance. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its clinical relevance.

We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024.

title: AI Applications in Aortic and Peripheral Artery Disease: Risk Prediction, Imaging, Procedural Support, and Longitudinal Surveillance.
abstract: Aortic disease and lower-extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) generate substantial morbidity, mortality, and longitudinal imaging burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly studied for vascular risk prediction, image analysis, procedural support, and surveillance, but the maturity of these applications is heterogeneous. This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit. Automated image segmentation and opportunistic abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) detection have the most mature evidence base, including retrospective external validation and, for AI-assisted AAA case finding, nonrandomized evidence of improved downstream evaluation and follow-up. Conversely, while machine-learning models for vascular risk prediction and disease progression often report high retrospective accuracy, their clinical readiness remains strictly investigational. Across most aortic and PAD applications, there is a persistent lack of independent external validation, decision-curve analysis, and prospective testing against standard care. Image-fusion guidance has clinical evidence for reducing procedural resource use, but this evidence should not be conflated with autonomous AI or robotic navigation. Cardiovascular digital twins remain largely mechanistic, computational, or early-development frameworks. AI can augment vascular imaging and risk assessment, but high retrospective accuracy is not equivalent to clinical utility. Current guideline thresholds for repair, revascularization, and surveillance should not be altered on the basis of investigational radiomics or prediction models. Translation requires multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration and net-benefit assessment, transparent reporting, and trials demonstrating improved patient outcomes.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk.

RESULTS: At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher-versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher-versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792).

CONCLUSIONS: Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

CENTRAL PICTURE: Multidimensional digital twin model stratifies aortic event-free survival in AUTBAD.

CENTRAL MESSAGE: Combining patient-specific 3D aortic morphology and wall stress may improve identification of medically managed AUTBAD patients at high risk for aortic intervention or aortic-related death.

PERSPECTIVE: TBAD geometry is highly patient specific, and one-dimensional measurements may not fully reflect patient risk. Digital twin modeling incorporating 3D morphology and wall mechanics may provide a more complete basis for risk stratification. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating multidimensional shape and stress data into a risk-stratification model to identify high-risk AUTBAD patients.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed.

title: Endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs).

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients were diagnosed with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). Twelve underwent endovascular treatment following definitive diagnosis by digital subtraction angiography (DSA); two declined intervention despite confirmed diagnosis. Thirteen presented with predominant ocular manifestations-such as proptosis, chemosis, and ophthalmoparesis-while one was diagnosed incidentally on cranial MRI performed for headache and dizziness. All 12 patients underwent the procedure successfully: seven underwent arterial-access embolization and five underwent venous-access embolization. Onyx liquid embolic agent was used as the sole embolic material in seven cases; in the remaining five cases, detachable coils were employed as adjunctive agents. Immediate post-procedural DSA demonstrated complete occlusion in nine patients and subtotal occlusion in three. Procedure-related complications occurred in five patients: visual acuity reduction (n = 2), ipsilateral facial hypoesthesia (n = 2), and isolated impairment of abduction and downward gaze (n = 1). Symptomatic improvement was observed in seven patients. At 1-year clinical and imaging follow-up, all 12 treated patients remained under surveillance. Ten exhibited no recurrence; notably, one patient with initial subtotal occlusion achieved complete angiographic occlusion during follow-up. In the remaining two, residual lesions remained stable in size, symptoms improved, and no secondary intervention was required. Among the five patients with procedure-related complications, two developed persistent facial hypoesthesia after intra-arterial embolization; subjective numbness gradually improved but did not fully resolve during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for craniospinal dural arteriovenous fistula (CSDAVFs) is associated with favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. Although procedure-related complications occur in a subset of patients, most are transient and resolve spontaneously or improve to partial remission during follow-up. Collectively, these findings support endovascular therapy as a safe and effective treatment modality for CSDAVFs.

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

title: Investigating the proportion of children with pulmonary embolism who have concomitant deep vein thrombosis reveals the hazards of observational data.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is thought to arise from a thrombus in a distant vein. In adults, concomitant deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is only found in about half of the patients with PE. There are no studies in children addressing this question. Because PE is a low prevalent disease in children, only observational data is available. This provides an opportunity to validate concerns regarding observational studies. This analysis compared four types of observational data: a single institution retrospective review, and case reports, small series, and large database studies identified from a formal systematic review. The proportion with concomitant DVT, age, sex, PE location, DVT location, mortality, and hospital versus community acquired were compared amongst the data sources. Amongst the 268 included studies, and 22,449 children with PE, 17.6% had concomitant DVT. There was wide variability in the estimate of the proportion who had concomitant DVT. In large databases, 15.7% had DVT, 31% from the single institution study, 47.3% from small series, and 63% from case reports. In the 29 small series, the proportion with concomitant DVT ranged from 0 to 89%. This study validates concerns regarding observational data in medicine. Because of this, the overall proportion of children with concomitant DVT determined by this study is likely inaccurate. However, it is reasonable to conclude that a significant proportion, and perhaps a majority of children with PE will not have concomitant DVT.

title: Rapid Infrarenal Aortic Rupture During Persistent Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteraemia: Serial CT Evolution and Staged Endovascular Treatment-A Case Report.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Persistent Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia can seed an atherosclerotic aorta. Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. Case Presentation: An 80-year-old woman (BMI 19.5 kg/m2) presented with hypogastric and lumbar pain. Multiphasic CT showed a calcified infrarenal aorta with periaortic inflammation but no haemorrhage. Blood cultures obtained on two occasions confirmed persistent methicillin-susceptible S. aureus bacteraemia. Interval CT angiography showed an enhancing circumferential cuff and a small anterior contrast focus without a definite ulcer crater. Eight days after the initial CT, hypotension developed; CT angiography showed focal aortic wall disruption, active extravasation, and a large retroperitoneal haematoma. Emergency aorto-bi-iliac EVAR controlled the bleeding. An inferior mesenteric artery-fed type II endoleak filled the fresh rupture cavity and was treated by coil embolisation via mesenteric collaterals. One-month CTA showed a patent graft without endoleak. At six weeks, the patient remained clinically well with healed wounds and no need for further vascular intervention. CRP fell from 148.1 mg/L on postoperative day 5 to 49.4 mg/L at six weeks and 24.2 mg/L at approximately 12 weeks; the next outpatient review was scheduled in three months, although microbiological clearance remained undocumented. Conclusions: Serial imaging and persistent MSSA bacteraemia support probable infective aortitis with focal wall disruption; an infected degenerative PAU remains possible. Persistent bacteraemia, focal pain, and a progressive periaortic cuff should prompt early vascular review and short-interval imaging.

Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. title: Noninvasive electrical impedance tomography monitoring during total aortic arch replacement: incremental value for prediction of postoperative neurological deficit.
abstract: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR. Methods: A 16-electrode EIT system and NIRS were utilized for intraoperative cerebral neuromonitoring during TAAR. Correlations between intraoperative EIT and NIRS variables and postoperative ND were comprehensively analyzed. Results: The overall incidence of postoperative ND was 39.1% (59/151), including a 15.2% incidence of postoperative stroke. The time integral of absolute resistivity asymmetry index during hypothermic circulatory arrest (TRAIHCA), the maximum absolute resistivity asymmetry ratio during HCA (MRARHCA), age, body mass index, supra-aortic branch involvement, and operative duration were independent predictors of postoperative ND. Incorporation of EIT parameters into the clinical prediction model significantly improved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.752 to 0.817 (P = 0.027). Moreover, the incremental prognostic value of EIT was further validated by improved risk reclassification and discriminatory ability for ND, with a net reclassification index of 0.510 (P = 0.002) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.072 (P < 0.001). Conclusion: The EIT parameters have been demonstrated to be an effective means of predicting ND following TAAR. Cerebral EIT may represent a potential alternative for intraoperative noninvasive multimodal neuromonitoring options.
englishSummary: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR.

title: Intraoperative measurement of the ascending aortic diameter at the onset of aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior studies have associated aortic size with dissection risk, none have corrected for dissection-related aortic expansion. This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection.

METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation. In this study, the intimal lumen diameter measured at its maximal stretching state was used as a reliable surrogate for the pre-dissection aortic diameter. Subsequently, the relationship between this surrogate and the aortic diameter measured on post-dissection CT at the corresponding levels was further analyzed.

RESULTS: Using this method, the pre-dissection ascending aortic diameter was measured as 37.5 ± 6.6 mm, whereas the post-dissection CT measurement at the same level increased to 43.9 ± 7.0 mm. After excluding patients with non-A-non-B aortic dissection, the mean ascending aortic diameter increased by approximately 20% after dissection compared with the pre-dissection value, corresponding to an absolute increase of 7.5 mm in diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: Although aortic diameter remains a robust indicator for prophylactic surgery in the study population, acute aortic dissection is seldom associated with true ascending aortic aneurysms and occurs with normal or near-normal aortic dimensions in most patients. When dissection occurs in the setting of a small aortic diameter, it likely reflects a profound functional vulnerability of the aortic tissue to catastrophic aortic events.

This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection. METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation.

title: Oral anticoagulants and the risk of acute kidney injury: a retrospective real-world cohort study using overlap propensity score weighting.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Overlap propensity score weighting, with weights derived from a generalized boosted model incorporating 81 baseline covariates, balanced the treatment groups. Weighted logistic regression compared the risk of AKI within 30 days of OAC initiation, defined by KDIGO criteria. Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and logistic regression-derived overlap weighting, each with or without doubly robust covariate adjustment.

RESULTS: Among 6 876 patients (5 048 DOAC users; 1 828 warfarin users), DOAC initiation was associated with a higher risk of AKI than warfarin after overlap weighting (OR: 1.346, 95% CI: 1.057-1.715; p = 0.016), and with severe AKI (stage 2-3; OR: 1.694, 95% CI: 1.013-2.832; p = 0.044), whereas stage 1 AKI did not differ significantly. The association persisted after additional covariate adjustment (OR: 1.363, 95% CI: 1.068-1.740; p = 0.013) and across alternative propensity score models, although the unadjusted IPTW model did not. By indication, the association was significant for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) (OR: 1.566, 95% CI: 1.034-2.369; p = 0.034) but not for venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment or prophylaxis. Among individual DOACs, rivaroxaban was associated with an elevated risk (OR: 1.392, 95% CI: 1.075-1.804; p = 0.012), whereas edoxaban, dabigatran, and apixaban were not. Lower-dose rivaroxaban initiation was associated with an increased risk (OR: 2.792, 95% CI: 1.524-5.114; p = 0.001), whereas higher-dose and off-label use were not. In prespecified subgroup analyses, ORs were above 1 in most strata, but most comparisons were not significant, and no significant interactions were detected.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, may be associated with a higher short-term risk of AKI than warfarin. Given the expanding use of DOACs, medication-specific renal effects warrant further investigation, and close monitoring of renal function may be advisable in high-risk patients after anticoagulation initiation.

However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.

title: Molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers of Type B aortic dissection risk in Marfan syndrome: a scoping review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused primarily by pathogenic FBN1 variants, with aortic dissection a leading cause of mortality. Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and the framework of Arksey and O'Malley. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for articles published between January 2010 and October 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and scored each study for evidence certainty across six domains.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies met criteria, derived from 14 independent source populations; eight came from a single Dutch cohort network. Only two studies reported Type B dissection as a specified outcome; the remainder addressed dissection of unspecified type, aortic diameter or growth, or mechanistic endpoints. Four thematic evidence streams emerged. TGF-β pathway biomarkers show associations with aortic phenotype and disease severity across several cohorts, but their value for prospective prediction of Type B dissection remains unvalidated. Variants in TGFBR2 and TGFB2, and FBN1 cysteine-loss variants, are associated with severe aortic phenotypes yet are not integrated into the Ghent nosology. Losartan shows heterogeneous efficacy, and a predefined randomized trial substudy suggests that benefit may depend on FBN1 variant class, although no trial has stratified outcomes by dissection type. No tool exists to stratify Type B risk in the 5 to 10 percent of clinically diagnosed patients without an identifiable FBN1 variant. Evidence certainty was moderate for the pharmacologic stream and low to very low for the other three, and the biomarker evidence is associational rather than causal.

CONCLUSIONS: A competing-risks multimodal model integrating imaging, genotype, and treatment-adjusted biomarker trajectory, developed and externally validated in multicentre prospective cohorts, represents the next research frontier.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused primarily by pathogenic FBN1 variants, with aortic dissection a leading cause of mortality. Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

title: Application of endovascular stent graft in ABO-incompatible living donor kidney transplantation: a case report.
abstract: Severe iliac arteriosclerosis is a contraindication for kidney transplantation (KT). This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively. Routine pre-transplant therapy including rituximab 200mg, triple immunosuppressants included tacrolimus (7mg/d, tacrolimus concentration was between 3.8 and 9.2 ng/mL), mycophenolate mofetil (1500mg/d), methylprednisolone (16mg/d). Following one session of double filtration plasmapheresis, anti-blood group antibody titers were reduced 1:4 and 1:8 for IgG and IgM. Two days prior to surgery, patient underwent one session of plasma exchange and antibody titers were IgG 1:4 and IgM 1:8 on the day of KT. Basiliximab was administered for immune induction. The initial routine was performed with conventional end-to-side anastomosis between the renal graft artery and the right external iliac artery. However, pulsation of the transplant renal artery disappeared shortly. Upon opening the anastomosis, thrombosis at the anastomotic site was identified due to plaque embolism from the external iliac artery. Consequently, a self-expandable endovascular covered stent was implanted into the external iliac artery via the right femoral artery under intervention. Because part of the external iliac artery wall was defective, the endovascular stent was partially exposed, used the prosthetic graft for coverage and reinforcement. Finally, the renal allograft artery was anastomosed end-to-side to the stent-prosthetic complex. The anti-blood group antibody titers were 1:2 and 1:4 for IgG and IgM and serum creatinine was 124 μmol/L at 1 month. During the 2 years follow-up, graft function remained satisfactory, the serum creatinine levels were 116, 107, and 113 μmol/L at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively, and no signs of right lower limb ischemia were evident. This study demonstrates that renal graft implanted on the endovascular stent is a feasible therapeutic option for recipients with severe iliac arteriosclerosis.

This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively.

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R.

RESULTS: BAFF-R on CD20- (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797-0.926, P = 7.17 × 10-5) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843-0.961, P = 1.57 × 10-3) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs.

CONCLUSION: This multi-omics genetic-toxicology study provides causal genetic evidence for immune-metabolite regulatory axes in AA pathogenesis. Notably, Adrenate presents dual biological effects: it transmits immune-protective signals but exerts direct vascular cellular toxicity. Our findings highlight the utility of MR-assisted precision toxicity prediction for disease risk evaluation and therapeutic target mining for AA.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls.

title: Ginkgo biloba Extract for Intermittent Claudication in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Intermittent claudication (IC) secondary to peripheral artery disease (PAD) causes exertional leg pain and discomfort, which limits functional walking capacity. The clinical efficacy of Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) as a therapeutic agent for IC is debatable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GBE compared with a placebo in patients with IC due to PAD. Methods: Databases including PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CINAHL were searched until 24 April 2026. Eligible studies included randomized, double-blind, controlled trials (RCTs) comparing placebo. Primary outcome was absolute claudication distance (ACD) at the end of the study. Secondary outcomes were initial claudication distance (ICD), ankle-brachial index (ABI), ankle pressure, and adverse events. Walking outcomes across various treadmill protocols were standardized to estimate caloric expenditure (kcal). A random-effects model was used to pool the effect estimates across trials. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2). Results: A total of 14 RCTs comprising 893 participants represent the total number randomized were included. GBE was associated with a statistically significant but modest improvement in ACD compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], 3.50 kcal; 95% CI, 0.02 to 6.98; p = 0.049). This benefit was significant in trials with a 24-week duration (MD, 4.67 kcal; 95% CI, 2.26 to 7.08; p < 0.001) but not in 12-16 weeks trials (MD, 1.35 kcal; 95% CI, -2.39 to 5.09; p = 0.48). No significant changes were observed for ICD or resting ABI/ankle pressure. GBE was well tolerated, with an overall adverse event incidence comparable to placebo. Conclusions: In patients with IC due to PAD, GBE therapy improves absolute walking performance, with a significant effect observed in trials evaluating 24 weeks of treatment. Given its favorable safety and tolerability profile, GBE can represent a clinically relevant and well-tolerated therapeutic option to support functional walking capacity, particularly for patients unable to tolerate or use conventional pharmacological agents.
englishSummary: Background/Objectives: Intermittent claudication (IC) secondary to peripheral artery disease (PAD) causes exertional leg pain and discomfort, which limits functional walking capacity. The clinical efficacy of Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) as a therapeutic agent for IC is debatable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GBE compared with a placebo in patients with IC due to PAD.

title: N-Butyl Cyanoacrylate Use for the Management of Type II Endoleak in Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Objective: Different endovascular techniques are available for type II endoleak management. This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A protocol was registered on Open Science Framework. A systematic search using the PCC (Population, Concept, Context) framework was performed in PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library. Findings were systematically presented using structured tables summarizing NBCA techniques, efficacy and safety outcomes. Results: Following full-text assessment, 65 studies were included, comprising cohort and comparative studies, case reports, technical reports and preclinical studies. Single-arm cohort studies reported technical success rates of 90-100%, complication rates of 0-40% and variable durability outcomes, with clinical success ranging from 88 to 100%, endoleak resolution from 40 to 100% and aneurysm sac increase from 13 to 50%. Comparative studies reported improved outcomes with ethanol addition to the NBCA-ethiodized oil mixture compared with NBCA-ethiodized oil alone, shorter procedure times with direct puncture versus intra-arterial approach and more durable mid-term outcomes with selective embolization of contributing branches. Individually reported complications highlighted embolization risks and technical reports focused on catheter utilization. Pre-emptive embolization showed favorable outcomes on sac diameter reduction and endoleak type II occurrence. Conclusions: NBCA demonstrated technical feasibility for type II endoleak management, with variable durability. Considerable heterogeneity existed in access techniques, mixture ratios and outcome reporting. Preventive use demonstrated promising outcomes. Given the retrospective designs, limited sample sizes and heterogenous outcomes, adequately powered prospective studies are warranted.
englishSummary: Objective: Different endovascular techniques are available for type II endoleak management. This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

title: Secondary TEVAR After Frozen Elephant Trunk: Indications and Timing.
abstract: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) stabilizes the arch and proximal descending aorta, but complete distal remodeling is achieved in only a subset of patients with aortic dissection. Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET. PubMed was searched to September 2026, and 97 publications were included. Evidence obtained in patients treated with FET is distinguished from evidence extrapolated from primary type B dissection and from the authors' interpretation. We summarize the predictors of incomplete remodeling, including stent graft length, residual re-entry location, chronicity, aortic diameter at the distal stent level, early remodeling trajectory, and heritable aortopathy, and we contrast planned completion with surveillance-based reactive TEVAR, including technical aspects and spinal cord protection. Direct evidence on timing after FET is limited to retrospective series and one pilot randomized trial of TEVAR 1 to 3 months after type I repair; most data on the time-dependent loss of flap plasticity come from primary type B dissection. No universal timing rule is supported. We propose a phenotype-driven approach, not yet validated, in which timing is referenced to dissection onset and individualized to aortic anatomy, disease progression, and clinical condition.

Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET.

title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2).

RESULTS: Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

CONCLUSION: Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.

We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT.

title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

title: Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear dose-response meta-analysis, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 22% higher risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.37; p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall dose-response association (p = 0.001) with no evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.367), indicating an approximately linear relationship between the TyG index and PAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is associated with an increased risk of incident PAD in a dose-dependent and approximately linear manner.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261470450.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention.

KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images.

title: "Inflammation-Thrombosis Dissociation": a retrospective study of early DVT differences after UKA between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3. Demographic characteristics, platelet count, hemoglobin, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were collected. Propensity score matching was used to control differences in age, sex, and body mass index, and Firth logistic regression was used to analyze factors associated with DVT.

RESULTS: Among the 147 patients, 14 developed postoperative DVT, for an overall incidence of 9.52%. The DVT incidence was 4.30% (4/93) in Tibetan patients, lower than the 18.52% (10/54) observed in Han Chinese patients (P = 0.007). Platelet count, D-dimer, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were all higher in Tibetan than in Han Chinese patients; however, these higher values did not correspond to a higher DVT incidence. After 1:1 matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 16 matched pairs were obtained; DVT incidences were 18.8% in Han Chinese patients and 0% in Tibetan patients. The difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.250), although the direction of the association was consistent with that before matching. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression showed that increasing age was associated with higher odds of DVT in Model 2 (OR = 1.110, 95% CI: 1.028-1.211, P = 0.007). In the primary model adjusted for age and BMI (Model 3), Tibetan ethnicity was associated with lower odds of DVT than Han Chinese ethnicity (OR = 0.206, 95% CI: 0.038-0.948, P = 0.042). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for sex (Model 4: OR = 0.243, 95% CI: 0.040-1.376, P = 0.109). In exploratory models separately incorporating postoperative platelet count, D-dimer, systemic immune-inflammation index, or aggregate index of systemic inflammation (Models 5-8), the association between ethnicity and DVT remained statistically significant (all P < 0.05), whereas none of these laboratory indices showed a statistically significant association with DVT (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among high-altitude UKA patients receiving a uniform aspirin prophylaxis regimen, Han Chinese patients had a higher incidence of early postoperative DVT than Tibetan patients. Although Tibetan patients had higher platelet counts and composite inflammatory indices, these measures did not increase in parallel with DVT events, suggesting a possible dissociation between inflammatory phenotype and clinical thrombotic risk among different ethnic groups at high altitude. Age and ethnicity were relatively stable DVT-associated factors in this cohort, whereas platelet count, D-dimer, and platelet-inflammation composite indices were insufficient to explain the between-ethnicity difference in risk. Given the single-center retrospective design and the limited number of outcome events and matched patients, these findings require further validation in multicenter, large-sample prospective studies.

title: Modified Hybrid Repair with Open Reconstruction of Infrarenal Aortoiliac Segment for Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms Without Custom Distal Landing Zone: A Single-Center Case Series.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate distal landing zones can limit hybrid repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA). We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025. Open aneurysm excision and aortoiliac reconstruction provided the distal sealing segment and inflow for visceral and renal bypasses. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative length of hospital stay, 30-day major complication rate, 30-day paraplegia rate, 1-year reintervention rate, 30-day readmission rate, and technical success rate. Results: Five patients had Crawford extent II aneurysms and four had extent III aneurysms. Technical success was achieved in all nine patients. Median operative time, estimated blood loss, and intensive care unit stay were 724 min, 2500 mL, and 8 days, respectively. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 0% (0/9). No spinal cord ischemia or mesenteric ischemia occurred within 30 days. Acute kidney injury occurred in six patients (66.7%), including one who received continuous renal replacement therapy. One patient required early covered stent-graft repair of a right iliac anastomotic leak. At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6-12), all reconstructed visceral and renal bypasses were patent, no new endoleak was detected, and all patients were alive. No additional reintervention was required. Conclusions: Modified hybrid repair with prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction was technically feasible in selected TAAA patients with inadequate distal sealing anatomy. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to evaluate durability and refine indications.

title: Age-specific associations of endovascular therapy and reperfusion delay with outcomes after large vessel occlusion: a regional registry study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years. The primary outcome was an ordinal shift towards a better 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes were dichotomized functional measures incorporating prestroke status.

RESULTS: Among 837 patients younger than 85 years, EVT was associated with a favourable mRS shift (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.01). Among 443 patients aged 85 years or older, the estimate was favourable but not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.87-1.92). No significant age-by-treatment interaction was observed for functional outcomes. Among patients treated with successful reperfusion by EVT, favourable outcomes declined more steeply with increasing onset-to-reperfusion time in those aged 85 years or older.

DISCUSSION: The association of EVT with functional outcomes was not significantly modified by age but estimates in very elderly patients were less precise. Very elderly patients appeared more vulnerable to reperfusion delay.

CONCLUSION: Treatment selection should integrate prestroke function, stroke severity, imaging findings, procedural feasibility, and the likelihood of rapid reperfusion rather than age alone.

We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for the detection of acute aortic syndrome in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic disorders with a wide range of presentations that are easily misdiagnosed in the emergency department (ED). The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines recommended focused transthoracic echocardiography as the first-line imaging tool for the detection of aortic dissection, but the performance of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in detecting AAS in ED varies considerably in the existing literature. We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting. METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies of POCUS in the ED for the detection of AAS were included. For included studies, the diagnostic accuracy of POCUS for detecting AAS was revealed by calculating the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio, and diagnostic odds ratio, with 95% credible intervals (CrI). The diagnostic performance of POCUS was evaluated by summary receiver operator curve (SROC). RESULTS: A total of 4,855 patients from seven studies were included in the meta-analysis. For any sonographic signs for detecting AAS, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of POCUS were 88.3% (95%CrI: 85.1% -91.2%) and 80.3% (95%CrI: 63.4%-92.9%), respectively. The area under the SROC of any sonographic signs for detecting AAS was 0.91 (95%CrI: 0.65-0.96). CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides support that POCUS may be a useful early imaging tool for ruling in AAS in the ED due to its high specificity for direct sonographic sign. While the overall certainty of evidence is moderate to low, larger-scale prospective studies on the use of POCUS with other diagnostic tools for detecting AAS are necessary in ED settings.

We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting.

title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.

This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.

To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.
