title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023.

title: Development and Psychometric Validation of a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Questionnaire on Pulmonary Embolism and Its Modifiable Risk Factors (PE-KAP-RO): Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study in Adults from Western Romania.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), whose most severe manifestation is pulmonary embolism (PE), is the third most common acute cardiovascular disorder, and many of its risk factors≠-obesity, physical inactivity, smoking, and unfavorable dietary patterns-are modifiable. No validated instrument is currently available to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding PE among adults in Romania, and the burden of self-reported thromboembolic risk factors in community settings has not been described with standardized measures. This protocol describes the development and psychometric validation of the PE-KAP-RO questionnaire, an integrated assessment tool comprising three scored KAP scales, three embedded validated lifestyle instruments, and an exploratory, unweighted VTE risk-factor burden index. No participants had been enrolled and no data had been collected at the time of submission; all procedures are therefore described as planned.

METHODS: The study comprises two phases. Phase 1 (development) includes qualitative concept elicitation with members of the target population, guideline- and theory-anchored item generation, expert content validation quantified by the content validity index, and pilot testing with cognitive debriefing (n ≈ 30). Phase 2 is a cross-sectional field validation in at least 450 adults (≥18 years) from Western Romania-with recruitment continuing toward 600 where feasible-through combined in-person (quota-guided) and online sampling that includes healthcare professionals, with test-retest re-administration in a subsample of at least 60 participants after 14 ± 4 days. Physical activity, diet, and nicotine dependence will be measured with the IPAQ-SF, MEDAS, and FTND. Sample size is justified separately for each analysis (precision of proportions, correlation and regression power, events per variable, split-sample factor analysis, item response theory calibration, and reliability estimation). Measurement properties will be evaluated against pre-specified acceptance criteria: item difficulty 0.20-0.80 (a screening range interpreted together with discrimination) and corrected item-total correlations ≥ 0.30; internal consistency (KR-20/Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega) 0.70-0.95; test-retest ICC ≥ 0.70 and item-level weighted kappa ≥ 0.60; structural validity by split-sample exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis (CFI/TLI ≥ 0.90, RMSEA ≤ 0.08, SRMR ≤ 0.08); item response theory calibration with formal model comparison and differential item functioning screening; construct validity requiring confirmation of ≥75% of a priori hypotheses; floor/ceiling effects < 15%; and measurement invariance across sex, age group, and administration mode.

EXPECTED RESULTS: The study will deliver a validated Romanian-language instrument, a structured characterization of PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and preventive practices, and the distribution of self-reported risk factors in the study sample.

CONCLUSIONS: PE-KAP-RO is intended as a standardized assessment tool for PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices; the risk-factor burden index is descriptive and does not estimate VTE probability; any future predictive tool would require a separate cohort followed for incident VTE. Reporting follows the STROBE recommendations and COSMIN-based methodology; the protocol is presented prior to participant enrollment.

title: A Vascular Surgery and Primary Care Partnership for Improving Resident Training in Peripheral Artery Disease Management.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis, establishment of best medical management, and timely specialty referral for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain ongoing challenges. In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care.

METHODS: A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions. A presession survey assessed self-rated knowledge, practices, attitudes, and medical training regarding PAD, followed by a truncated postsession survey. The responses were grouped as high versus moderate/low. Descriptive statistics and the McNemar Exact test were used for paired sample comparison.

RESULTS: Thirty-one residents completed both surveys (65% IM, 35% FM, 58% male, and 77% first- or second-year trainees). Presession data revealed gaps in knowledge with few residents rating their understanding as "high". Postsession, there was a significant increase across all measured areas (P < 0.001). Notably, improvements were seen in the number of residents who felt highly confident in diagnosing PAD (from 16.1% to 90.3%), using a vascular Doppler (6.5% to 83.9%), ordering noninvasive testing (from 6.5% to 83.9%), performing a lower extremity pulse exam (from 12.9% to 87.1%), managing PAD for amputation prevention (from 12.9% to 71.0%), and referring to a vascular specialist (from 25.8% to 83.9%).

CONCLUSION: Resident knowledge and confidence improved significantly as a result of a singular educational session. This collaborative model between vascular surgery educators and primary care residency programs demonstrates an adaptable framework that successfully addresses a gap in PAD management training.

title: Calibrated Microspheres versus Liquid Embolic Agents for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Single-Center Clinicoradiologic Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAe) is an effective treatment for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), but the optimal embolic agent remains debated. Landmark randomized trials predominantly used liquid embolics, although calibrated microspheres remain widely used. We compared clinicoradiologic outcomes after MMAe with 75 μm Embozene microspheres versus liquid embolics (n-butyl cyanoacrylate or Onyx 18).

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed single-agent MMAe for cSDH at a tertiary center (January 2019-January 2025). The embolized MMA was the unit of analysis; agent choice was discretionary. The efficacy cohort required 2-8 week imaging (n = 66); the safety cohort included all single-agent procedures (n = 67; 35 particle, 32 liquid). Primary outcomes were embolization failure and unplanned surgical evacuation. Secondary outcomes included early SDH thickness, midline shift, and latest modified Rankin scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Fifty patients underwent 66 embolizations (16 bilateral): 34 particle and 32 liquid. Embolization failure occurred in 5/34 versus 4/32, and unplanned evacuation in 3/34 versus 1/32; events were few and the comparison underpowered. Female patients were more frequent in the particle group (47% vs. 19%, P = 0.020). Early SDH thickness was 8 (6) versus 6 (6) mm (P = 0.340). The safety cohort had one fatal posterior-circulation infarct after Embozene (1/35 vs. 0/32) and no other periprocedural complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Embolization failure was similar between 75 μm Embozene and liquid embolics, while unplanned evacuation was numerically higher with particles. Given infrequent events, limited sample size, and baseline imbalances, agent selection may be individualized by anatomy, visualization, and operator experience.

Landmark randomized trials predominantly used liquid embolics, although calibrated microspheres remain widely used. We compared clinicoradiologic outcomes after MMAe with 75 μm Embozene microspheres versus liquid embolics (n-butyl cyanoacrylate or Onyx 18).

title: Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Large Ruptured Isolated Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysm in a 98-Year-Old Patient: A Case Report.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Isolated internal iliac artery aneurysm (IIAA) is rare and carries a high mortality when ruptured. Management is particularly challenging in very elderly, anticoagulated patients in whom open repair may carry substantial perioperative risk. Herein, we report a case that illustrates device selection when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs. Case Presentation: A 98-year-old man receiving apixaban presented with lower abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea. Computed tomography demonstrated a ruptured right IIAA measuring 79 × 72 mm in the axial plane, with retroperitoneal hematoma. A marked size discrepancy between the common iliac artery (20 mm) and external iliac artery (approximately 10 mm), together with vessel tortuosity, made common iliac-external iliac bridging with an iliac limb unsuitable with the devices available. Emergency endovascular aneurysm repair with a full aortic bifurcated endograft was combined with coil embolization of the inferior gluteal artery and gelatin sponge embolization of the sac. The contralateral internal iliac artery, which harbored a 31 mm aneurysm, was preserved. A suspected type IV endoleak had resolved on CT at day 4, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 8 without complications. At 6-month follow-up, the aneurysm sac had decreased from 79 × 72 mm to 72 × 62 mm in the axial plane with no evidence of endoleak, and he remained ambulatory without pelvic ischemic symptoms. Conclusions: A full aortic bifurcated endograft combined with coil and sac embolization may be a feasible bail-out option when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs, even in a nonagenarian receiving apixaban.

Management is particularly challenging in very elderly, anticoagulated patients in whom open repair may carry substantial perioperative risk. Herein, we report a case that illustrates device selection when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Cannulation of Arteriovenous Fistulas in Hemodialysis Units: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis, but difficult or unsuccessful cannulation may cause pain, complications, and access dysfunction. This review evaluated whether ultrasound-guided cannulation improves outcomes compared with standard cannulation. Methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing ultrasound-guided and standard arteriovenous fistula cannulation in hemodialysis patients. Findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Of 1210 records identified, five randomized trials involving 142 patients were included. Some trials reported improved cannulation success or lower pain with ultrasound guidance, but findings varied across populations and outcome measures. Three of four trials reporting procedure time found longer durations with ultrasound guidance. A consistent reduction in complications or improvement in patient satisfaction was not established. Staff findings mainly concerned confidence and acceptability. The certainty of evidence was low. Conclusions: The effects of ultrasound-guided AVF cannulation on pain varied across trials. These uncertain findings should be interpreted alongside the longer procedure times reported in several trials. Larger randomized trials with clearly defined outcomes and analyses accounting for repeated observations are needed before recommending routine use.

This review evaluated whether ultrasound-guided cannulation improves outcomes compared with standard cannulation. Methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines.

title: Preprocedural Serum Albumin and Early Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury After Elective Carotid Artery Stenting: Incremental Prognostic Information Beyond the PCI-Derived Mehran Score.
abstract: Background/Objectives: We assessed whether preprocedural serum albumin adds prognostic information to the PCI-derived Mehran score for early contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after elective carotid artery stenting (CAS). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included 121 consecutive elective patients (January 2020-April 2026). The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance. Because the score uses actual contrast volume, the combined model applies only after CAS. The outcome used KDIGO serum creatinine thresholds (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5 times baseline) from routine second-day testing. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: Early CA-AKI occurred in 32 patients (26.4%). Adjusted odds ratios were 1.35 per Mehran point (95% CI 1.13-1.60) and 11.68 for albumin < 3.5 g/dL (95% CI 4.14-32.97). AUC increased from 0.768 to 0.865 (95% CI 0.794-0.937; likelihood ratio χ2 = 24.58, p < 0.001). Corrected AUC, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.860, 0.96, and 0.132. In exploratory decision curves (20% threshold), corrected net benefit was 0.168 for the combined model and 0.133 for Mehran alone. Conclusions: Low preprocedural albumin added prognostic information to the PCI-derived score and may help select patients for closer renal surveillance after CAS. External validation and prospective impact studies are needed before clinical use.

The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions.

RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced.

CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes and Disease-Specific Quality of Life After Surgical and Conservative Treatments for Lower Limb Varicose Veins: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Lower limb varicose veins are a common manifestation of chronic venous disease and can adversely affect physical functioning, symptom burden, and disease-specific quality of life (QoL). Although high ligation and stripping have traditionally been considered standard surgical approaches, conservative and minimally invasive options, such as compression therapy, sclerotherapy, and endovenous thermal or non-thermal techniques, have increasingly gained prominence. However, comparative evidence regarding patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) remains heterogeneous and dispersed across randomized trials. This systematic review aimed to evaluate randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2016 and 2026 that compared surgical with conservative or minimally invasive interventions for lower limb varicose veins, with particular emphasis on patient-reported and disease-specific QoL outcomes. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Scopus, Web of Science, Excerpta Medica database (Embase), the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched for eligible RCTs published from January 2016 to July 2026. Studies evaluating surgical versus conservative or minimally invasive management and reporting PROMs or disease-specific QoL outcomes were included. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidance. Fourteen RCTs met the eligibility criteria. Interventions included open surgery, endovenous laser ablation (EVLA), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), mechanochemical ablation (MOCA), cyanoacrylate adhesive closure, ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS), and compression therapy. Improvements in disease-specific QoL and PROMs were reported from baseline in most treatment groups. However, these within-group improvements did not necessarily indicate superiority over alternative treatments. Between-group differences in QoL outcomes were generally small and inconsistent, although some trials reported differences in procedural pain, anatomical outcomes, or the need for re-intervention. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively. Surgical, conservative, and minimally invasive approaches were associated with meaningful improvements in patient-reported and disease-specific QoL, with no consistent evidence demonstrating clear superiority of one modality. Treatment decisions should therefore incorporate anatomical suitability, patient preference, procedural morbidity, potential need for re-intervention, and healthcare resource considerations alongside QoL outcomes.

However, comparative evidence regarding patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) remains heterogeneous and dispersed across randomized trials.

title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA. Materials and Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE). Secondary outcomes included pulmonary embolism (PE), proximal and distal DVT, bleeding outcomes, wound complications, blood transfusion, and mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Additional risk-difference sensitivity analyses incorporated CRISTAL's published cluster-adjusted estimates. Results: Sixteen trials involving 21,265 participants were included. Aspirin was associated with higher risks of symptomatic DVT (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.35-2.38), symptomatic VTE (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.33-2.18), PE (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.33-2.68), and distal DVT (RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.06-2.06). Aspirin was associated with lower risks of minor bleeding (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.71) and ecchymosis or bruising (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93). No statistically significant differences were detected for the other assessed outcomes. Additional analyses incorporating CRISTAL's cluster-adjusted risk differences did not identify statistically significant differences for the three primary outcomes or PE. Conclusions: The main pooled analyses associated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis with higher risks of symptomatic thromboembolic events. However, the symptomatic DVT and symptomatic VTE associations were no longer statistically significant after exclusion of CRISTAL or restriction to trials at low risk of bias. The low-risk analysis identified a significantly higher risk of any DVT with aspirin. Aspirin reduced minor bleeding and bruising without a statistically significant reduction in major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding. These findings require cautious interpretation given dependence on CRISTAL, sensitivity to trial inclusion and analytical approach, and differences in prophylactic strategies and outcome definitions.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm in the multicenter Reinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semiconversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results.

RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from endovascular AAA repair to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semiconversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semiconversion group [42.4% vs 86.8%; standard error, 0.04 vs standard error, 0.05; P < .001; log-rank, 15.9]. Conversion/semiconversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, whereas primary open treatment improved durability.

CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at 5 years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, whereas a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers.

title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear.

METHODS: NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory.

DISCUSSION: This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers.

RESULTS: Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P_interaction=0.028).

CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Caprini Score-Guided Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Spine Instrumentation Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Mechanical vs. Pharmacomechanical Strategies Across Etiological Subgroups.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), is a major source of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing spine surgery. Although various risk factors for developing VTE have been identified, pharmacological prophylaxis is used selectively in spine surgery due to the risk of epidural hematoma. We report our institutional experience with VTE prophylaxis following spine instrumentation surgery across all surgical etiologies.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients ≥18 years of age who underwent spine instrumentation surgery for degenerative, traumatic, or oncologic pathologies, and patients of all ages who underwent surgery for spinal deformity over a three-year period was performed. Caprini VTE risk score was used for individual risk stratification.

RESULTS: A total of 265 patients were included: degenerative (n=174, 65.7%), trauma (n=45, 17.0%), deformity (n=33, 12.5%), and tumor (n=13, 4.9%). The overall mean age was 46.1±17.5 years, and there were 133 male patients (50.2%). Significant differences existed across groups in age (Kruskal-Wallis H=97.4, p<0.001), index procedure characteristics, and VTE risk profiles. Mechanical prophylaxis alone was employed in 212 patients (80.0%), while 53 patients (20.0%) received combined pharmacomechanical prophylaxis. No patient (0%) in the mechanical-only group developed a perioperative VTE event or postoperative hematoma. One patient (1.9%) in the combined pharmacomechanical group developed a postoperative PE, arising in the context of a preoperative proximal DVT. Firth's penalized logistic regression identified polytrauma (OR 29.0, 95% CI 3.3-3835.0; p=0.001), Caprini score ≥7 (OR 8.8, 95% CI 3.8-20.9; p<0.001), and prior VTE history (OR 61.8, 95% CI 5.7-8406.4; p<0.001) as independent predictors of combined prophylaxis receipt.

CONCLUSION: Mechanical prophylaxis, implemented as part of a structured protocol that included sequential pneumatic compression devices and standardized postoperative care, was associated with low VTE risk following spine instrumentation surgery. Individualized risk stratification using validated tools such as the Caprini score, combined with selective pharmacomechanical prophylaxis in high-risk patients, may optimize outcomes in this population. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

Although various risk factors for developing VTE have been identified, pharmacological prophylaxis is used selectively in spine surgery due to the risk of epidural hematoma. We report our institutional experience with VTE prophylaxis following spine instrumentation surgery across all surgical etiologies.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device (IVID; InVera Medical) is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during nonthermal, nontumescent ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome.

METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes based on a Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI) symptom questionnaire, and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 and 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months postprocedure. Baseline and 12-month postprocedures were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively.

RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted P = .03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: The IVID provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID.

title: Systematic review of devices, designs, and trials for the treatment of deep venous reflux.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. Although superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR.

METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis.

RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: eight human and seven animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration and external compression, with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7% to 100%, patency from 67% to 100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0% to 44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18% to 22% of select human cohorts. One perioperative death occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0% to 92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction end points despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By 1 year, pain had improved in up to 97% of patients; revised Venous Clinical Severity Scores decreased by 37% to 81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67% to 100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate end points in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite end points integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio is associated with early major amputation after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification.

Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set.

title: Expressing Needs and Concerns During Nursing Care: An Ethnographic Study of Patients Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: This focused ethnographic study aimed to explore how patients expressed their needs and concerns during nursing care while undergoing planned open repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Fieldwork was conducted in a vascular surgery ward at a Danish university hospital between December 2024 and August 2025. Ten patients admitted for planned open repair were followed during their inpatient stay through participant observation. The ethnographic record comprised 85 hours of observation and was analyzed using Spradley's Developmental Research Sequence within a hermeneutic interpretive orientation. The overall cultural theme identified was "Expressing vulnerability while trying not to be a burden." This theme captures how physical recovery needs were more readily expressed, whereas emotional and existential concerns were softened, held back, or communicated through silence, humor, or reliance on family members. The included cases illustrate three domains: unspoken suffering as a barrier to well-being, family members' work in making patients' needs visible, and becoming dependent on nursing care as a patient. The findings show that patients undergoing open repair struggle to voice vulnerability directly during hospitalization. The study highlights the importance of nursing care that attends not only to explicit requests for help, but also to subtle verbal, embodied, and relational expressions of vulnerability.

title: Comparison of Midterm Outcomes of Different Patch Types for Endarterectomy of the Common Femoral Artery. Secondary Analysis from the ARISTON Multicenter Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to analyze patients who underwent femoral endarterectomy (FEA) for common femoral artery disease (CFAD) within the multicenter AtheRectomy-assIsted endovaScular Therapy versus OpeN (ARISTON) registry aiming to compare the short-term and midterm outcomes based on the use of different patch materials.

METHODS: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicenter observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary end point of the study was clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

RESULTS: A total of 547 patients undergoing FEA with patch angioplasty were included in the analysis and stratified according to the patch material into 3 groups: (i) prosthetic patch (PP; group A, n = 249), (ii) bovine pericardium patch (BPP; group B, n = 262), and (iii) great saphenous vein patch (GSVP; group C, n = 36). Baseline characteristics differed significantly among groups. Technical success of the FEA procedure was achieved in all cases. Perioperative mortality was low and not significantly different between groups. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from CD-TLR at 2 years were 86.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 80.8-90.2%) in the PP group, 88.9% (95% CI, 83.1-92.8%) in the BPP group, and 69.8% (95% CI, 49.3-83.3%) in the GSVP group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (log-rank P = 0.067). In multivariable analysis for freedom from CD-TLR, neither BPP (hazard ratio [HR] 0.78, 95% CI 0.47-1.29; P = 0.330) nor GSVP (HR 1.99, 95% CI 0.95-4.17; P = 0.069) was significantly associated with the outcome.

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary multicenter real-world experience, PP and BPP were the most used materials for patch reconstruction after FEA in patients with primary CFAD. Although the distribution of baseline risk factors was different between groups, midterm freedom from CD-TLR was not significantly different between groups. The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

title: Early stroke after aortic arch repair: Comparative and proportional meta-analyses of open, hybrid, and total endovascular strategies.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261461659).

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair [odds ratio, 1.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.46-8.58; P = .292; I2 = 52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair.

CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly noncomparative. Treatment should be individualized according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

title: ArtAssist sequential compression biomechanical device as a cost-dominant limb salvage strategy for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia: A decade and half, single-center cohort study with health economic and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive a median €88,820/patient; the long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device (SCBD) is lacking.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

RESULTS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (hazard ratio: 1.70, 1.80, 1.71; all P ≤ .012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = .008). Ninety-day rental (€1373/patient) reduced total expenditure sixfold vs primary amputation (€5.3M vs €30.8M), saving €76,500/patient. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity yielded a gain of 3.37 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) per patient; incremental cost-effectiveness ratio €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a sixfold reduction in costs vs primary amputation, +3.37 QALYs/patient, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-center cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for nonreconstructible CLTI.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.

METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty.

METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models.

RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05).

CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort.

title: Functional outcome after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury following thoracic aortic surgery.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of RLN injury and assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024. RLN injury was diagnosed by postoperative vocal cord paralysis. Aortic arch surgery included partial and total arch replacement, while thoracoabdominal surgery involved the proximal descending aorta. The primary end point was full voice recovery. Secondary end points included recovery of normal vocal cord mobility, residual dysphonia, the need for voice therapy, and vocal cord interventions.

RESULTS: Among 2983 patients undergoing aortic surgery, 70 (2.3%) were diagnosed with postoperative RLN injury. Median follow-up was 17 (interquartile range, 7-25) months. The incidence of RLN injury was 1.7% after arch surgery and 5.3% after thoracoabdominal procedures. At final follow-up, 34 patients (50%) achieved full voice recovery, while 20 (30%) had mild dysphonia, 9 (13%) moderate dysphonia, and 5 (7%) severe dysphonia. Voice therapy was performed in 49 (70%) patients, and 10 (14%) required additional vocal cord interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, the incidence of RLN injury after aortic surgery was lower than previously reported. Functional outcomes were favorable, with most patients achieving full or near-complete voice recovery through conservative or interventional management. Structured follow-up and multidisciplinary care remain essential to optimize outcomes after RLN injury.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of RLN injury and assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024.

title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%).

CONCLUSION: Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected.

title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease without Dedicated Guidelines.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695).

RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to zone 0 or 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, and none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost to follow-up (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (such as aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, and survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (zone 1-3; complete 56% vs incomplete/LTF 27%; P < .001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs incomplete/LTF 18%; P < .001), in-hospital thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension (7% vs 2%; P = .028), and thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs incomplete/LTF 5%; P = .002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete 12% vs incomplete 5%; P = .007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs 15%; P = .002) within 1-year of acute dissection. The long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete 97% vs incomplete 97% vs LTF 91%), 3-years (complete 92% vs incomplete 95% vs LTF 81%; P = .021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (P = .13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (hazard ratio, 2.87; 95% confidence interval, 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (hazard ratio, 2.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and midterm survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.
