title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.

METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

title: Real-life venous thromboembolism risk scores in multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment with daratumumab and lenalidomide has improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), however the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is high. Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort study.

METHODS: All consecutive MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and concomitant LMWH-ASA thromboprophylaxis between July, 2018 and September, 2023 were evaluated through chart review. Kaplan-Meier method and Concordance-Index (C-index) were used to estimate risk scores' prognostic accuracy.

RESULTS: 95 patients (median age 74 years) were included (n= 47 NTE-MM, and n= 48 RRMM). At 12 months from Dara-Rd initiation, 10 (10.4%) patients developed VTE; 4 (4.2%) had bleeding complications, and 2 (2.1%) patients died. Six VTE events (6.2%) occurred within first 6 months from Dara-Rd initiation while on LMWH prophylaxis, whereas 2 VTE (2%) developed in two patients receiving aspirin. The accuracy of IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM and EHR-CAT scores was generally poor, with C-Index values ranging from 0.43 (95% confidence intervals [95%CI] 0.30 to 0.56) to 0.53 (95%CI: 0.38 to 0.68). LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was completed by 89.5% of the cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-life cohort of MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and guideline-recommended antithrombotic prophylaxis, currently available VTE risk scores demonstrated moderate to poor prognostic accuracy. LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was feasible but associated with residual VTE risk.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

title: Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists for the treatment of venous thromboembolism in adults with sickle cell disease: a Bayesian meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing DOACs with VKAs in patients with SCD and VTE. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to March 2026. Primary outcomes were recurrent VTE and major bleeding (MB). Bayesian random-effects models with weakly informative priors were used to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Posterior probabilities were derived using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling.

RESULTS: Four retrospective studies including 271 patients (155 DOACs and 116 VKAs) were included. Recurrent VTE did not differ between groups (OR, 0.82; 95% CrI, 0.38-1.75), with a 67.1% posterior probability favoring DOACs, indicating equipoise. DOACs were associated with a significantly lower risk of MB (OR, 0.25; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.80), with a 99.2% probability of superiority. Between-study heterogeneity was low (τ = 0.15 for recurrent VTE; τ = 0.30 for MB).

CONCLUSION: DOACs demonstrate comparable efficacy to VKAs for preventing recurrent VTE in SCD, with a clinically meaningful reduction in MB. Given their safety profile and convenience, DOACs may be preferred; randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

title: Nongeneral Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals (PIs), and prespecified influence diagnostics.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with GA (risk ratio [RR] 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-1.52; I2≈86%; wide PI). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I2≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in intensive care unit stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

CONCLUSION: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to GA. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus.

title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort.

METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival.

RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.
englishSummary: AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort. METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed.

title: Clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism: secondary outcomes of the Hydra randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite its high prevalence, practice-based data on management and outcomes after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism (PE) are scarce, and no studies have investigated quality of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE.

METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer. Patients with PE at baseline or during 90-day follow-up were included in this study. Outcomes were recurrent venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life as assessed by the Pulmonary Embolism Quality of Life (PEmb-QoL) questionnaire. PEmb-QoL scores were compared with those for the general PE population reported in the FOCUS study. Lower scores indicate better QoL.

RESULTS: A total of 125 patients were included, of which 103 (82%) had PE at baseline, and 22 (18%) developed PE during follow-up. The 90-day cumulative incidence of recurrent venous thromboembolism and major bleeding was 2.5% (95% CI 0.67%-6.6%) and 2.5% (95% CI 0.68%-6.7%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 90 days was 32% (95% CI 23%-40%). Two-thirds of patients continued anticoagulation until less than 24 hours before death, and the median time between stopping anticoagulation and death was 10 days (IQR, 4-14). The median 90-day PEmb-QoL score was 33% (IQR, 13-51) versus 20% (IQR, 10-40) reported in the FOCUS study.

CONCLUSION: Patients with cancer-associated PE suffer from high mortality, high morbidity, and impaired quality of life. Anticoagulation therapy is frequently continued until the last days of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE. METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions.

METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years.

RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used.

CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]).

CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required.

title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.

METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and a COG5 Variant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis.

METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues.

RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 near HLA-A and rs9276409 within HLA-DQA2) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in the COG5 gene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted TPM4, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD.

CONCLUSIONS: This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidate COG5 variant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci.

title: Endovascular stenting of extracranial cervical artery dissections: A two-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Extracranial arterial dissections (EAD) are uncommon in the general population but represent a relatively frequent cause of ischemic stroke in young adults. Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-four EAD patients who underwent stenting were included. A standardized follow-up protocol at 12 months consisting of a clinical neurological assessment accompanied by imaging studies, including either Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Digital Subtraction Angiography was adopted.

RESULTS: In our cohort, most dissections were spontaneous (81 %) and predominantly involved the internal carotid artery (85 %), with acute stroke being the most common indication for stenting. Technical success was achieved in 85.7 % and complications occurred in 10 %. Three patients with initial stent implantation failure underwent successful secondary attempt. No significant predictors of technical success were identified. At discharge, good functional outcome was observed in 83 % of patients and at 12 months most followed patients showed favorable radiological results with high stent patency (86 %) and excellent clinical outcomes (mRS 0-2 in 97 %).

CONCLUSION: The results of our study suggest that for selected patients with medical therapy failure or hemodynamic compromise, stenting is a reasonable alternative. Given the limited evidence on indications, safety and efficacy, further randomized studies comparing stenting with medical management are warranted.

Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

title: Perceptions of decompressive craniectomy following endovascular thrombectomy in the Middle East and North Africa: A multi-specialty cross-sectional survey of attitudes, reported practices, and barriers.
abstract: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) can be a life-saving rescue therapy for malignant cerebral edema after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), yet DC practices following EVT have not previously been examined across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). We conducted a web-based, bilingual (English/Arabic) cross-sectional survey of physicians involved in acute stroke care across 15 MENA countries (January-March 2025) using a 22-item instrument that underwent expert content-validity review (S-CVI/UA = 0.86) and cognitive-interview pilot testing, to describe self-reported attitudes, perceived practices, and barriers regarding DC after EVT, and to determine whether key findings remained consistent among clinicians with the most direct relevant experience. Of 440 physicians invited, 179 responded; five respondents from zero-EVT-volume institutions were excluded, yielding an analytic cohort of 174 (response rate 41%) from 13 countries, of whom 49% (n = 85) were neurosurgeons. Eighty-four percent of respondents endorsed DC over medical management in selected patients, but only 51% perceived DC was performed in a timely manner "always/often." The mean physician-estimated, recall-based consent rate was 52% (SD 19%), with a Gulf Cooperation Council versus North African difference (59% vs. 44%, p < 0.001) that persisted when restricted to clinicians with direct family-meeting or operative involvement. Leading perceived barriers were patient/family preferences (79%), surgical resource constraints (55%), and delayed detection (30%). These findings, which reflect physician perceptions rather than institutionally verified practice, support development of culturally adapted consent pathways, standardized DC candidacy algorithms, regionalized stroke networks, and a prospective MENA stroke registry to confirm whether these perception-based signals correspond to actual clinical practice and outcomes.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.

title: Impact of prior antithrombotic therapy on safety and outcomes of endovascular therapy in large-core acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT.

RESULTS: A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n = 70; no ATD, n = 132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (pinteraction=0.944) or secondary outcomes (pinteraction=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited.

METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12.

DISCUSSION: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.Clinical Trial Registration: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP.

CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Faculty narrative feedback in the vascular surgery entrustable professional activity pilot is disproportionately focused on patient care and medical knowledge competencies.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity. It is unclear how faculty use this information to guide and focus the content of their feedback. We sought to identify the core competencies reflected in narrative feedback in a multi-institutional study of EPA assessments.

METHODS: EPA assessments were collected during a 3-month national Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. Trainees were rated on their performance of EPAs on a 4-point Likert scale and faculty had the opportunity to provide feedback. Narrative feedback was qualitatively analyzed using focused coding guided by the Vascular Surgery Milestones 2.0 framework. Feedback was coded using the six ACGME core competencies-patient care (PC), medical knowledge (MK), professionalism, interpersonal and communication skills, practice-based learning and improvement, and systems-based practice (SBP)-to characterize the domains emphasized in feedback. Quality assessment scores were assigned to all narrative feedback using the Quality of Assessment of Learning framework. Descriptive analysis was completed using R.

RESULTS: Faculty completed 983 EPA assessments of 78 trainees across 17 institutions (n = 16 integrated residencies, n = 12 fellowships). Narrative feedback was included in 760 (77%) assessments. Feedback most frequently addressed PC (n = 662, 82%), followed by MK (n = 418, 55%), whereas feedback about practice-based learning and improvement (n = 42, 6%), interpersonal and communication skills (n = 42,6%), professionalism (n = 20, 3%), and SBP (n = 26, 3%) were less common. Most assessments were completed for postgraduate year-3 (29%) and postgraduate year-4 trainees (22%). Most assessments occurred during the intraoperative phase of care (88%), with relatively few occurring in preoperative (7%) or postoperative (5%) phases. In addition, feedback-referencing PC was associated with higher odds of high-quality feedback in comparison with feedback about the other competencies (odds ratio, 25.56; 95% confidence interval, 6.13-106.55).

CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, faculty most frequently provided trainees with feedback on their performance of PC and MK competencies. Feedback on performance related to SBP was infrequently provided and, when provided, was of generally low quality. This has important implications for the use of EPAs to inform ACGME Milestones ratings and suggests alternative assessment tools will continue to be needed to capture performance across all competency domains required of a physician.

title: Impact of intravascular ultrasound guidance on radiation exposure during endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair: Single-center experience.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) in endovascular aortic aneurysms repair (EVAR) on reduction of radiation exposure.

METHODS: All EVAR procedures performed for symptomatic and asymptomatic infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms at a single U.K. center between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups based on imaging guidance used: IVUS-guided EVAR and standard EVAR. The primary end points were radiation dose and fluoroscopy time (FT), whereas the secondary outcomes included intraoperative technical success, change in pre- and postoperative serum creatinine level length of hospital stay, and 30-day morbidity and mortality.

RESULTS: During the study period, 51 patients met inclusion criteria at our center, 30 patients (58.8%) had standard EVAR procedure with fluoroscopy-guidance, whereas 21 patients (41.2%) had IVUS-guided EVAR procedure. Median dose area product in standard EVAR cases was 45.24 Gy cm2 compared with 7.27 Gy cm2 in IVUS-guided EVAR cases (P <.001, highly significant), and median FT in standard EVAR cases was 15.4 minutes compared with 4.5 minutes in IVUS-guided EVAR cases (P <.001, highly significant). Intraoperative technical success achieved in 19 patients (90%) in IVUS-guided cases compared with 28 patients (93%) in standard EVAR cases. The mean postoperative creatinine level was 71.4 ± 16.7 μmol/L in patients who underwent IVUS-guided EVAR cases, compared with 86.0 ± 22.0 μmol/L in patients with standard EVAR.

CONCLUSIONS: IVUS provides accurate and safe graft deployment while reducing the total radiation dose and FT. This significantly reduces the radiation risks to patients and staff while maintaining the highest patient care and procedure safety.

METHODS: All EVAR procedures performed for symptomatic and asymptomatic infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms at a single U.K. center between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: A Multicenter Case Review Program on the impact of ViTAA Regional Aortic Weakness Maps on clinical decision-making in abdominal aortic aneurysm management.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study, titled the ViTAA Case Review Program, aimed at evaluating the influence of the ViTAA Regional Aortic Weakness (RAW) Maps software on clinical decision-making in the management of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA). The purpose was twofold: first, to determine the impact of RAW Maps on projected patient care decisions compared with the standard of care approach, and second, to train investigators in the effective use of ViTAA RAW Maps for AAA assessment. This paper offers a case series focusing on the experience of participating surgeons in using the ViTAA RAW Maps software.

METHODS: Fifteen North American vascular surgeons participated and were provided with fully anonymized static and multiphase gated computed tomography angiography (CTA) scans obtained from a previous retrospective study. Five cases were selected from a single site and for each, participating physicians developed hypothetical treatment plans based on two imaging approaches: static CTA scans and multiphase gated CTA scans processed with the ViTAA RAW Maps software. These treatment plans were then compared to determine the impact of the ViTAA approach on clinical decision-making.

RESULTS: The ViTAA approach supported significantly higher surgical intervention rates compared with the standard of care, with vascular surgeons being 69% (P < .05) and 88% (P < .01) more likely to recommend surgery (either endovascular or open repair) at baseline and follow-up, respectively. The proportion of cases in which the recommendation changed when the ViTAA analysis was provided was 18.9% at baseline (95% confidence interval, 10.0-35.8) and 28.0% at follow-up (95% confidence interval, 19.1-41.0). ViTAA also prompted more endovascular aneurysm repair (72% more at baseline and 57% more at follow-up; P = .065 and P = .057, respectively), as well as increased fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (6.8% vs 2.7% at baseline and 11% vs 7% at follow-up; not statistically significant, P = .25 and P = .38, respectively). Across the 10 questionnaire items, 73% to 100% of participating physicians responded favorably to questions regarding the functionality and utility of the software.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that ViTAA technology may provide additional information for AAA risk stratification by incorporating functional image-derived biomechanical and hemodynamic metrics that offer deeper insight into aortic wall vulnerability. The participating physicians found these additional insights clinically meaningful, with the potential to influence management decisions for the reviewed cases. The usability of the software also suggests feasible integration into future workflows.

title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Upadacitinib in Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis: 5-Year Results from the Phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In the phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 study, treatment with upadacitinib (UPA), an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, improved signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) from weeks 12 through 152. We now report the long-term extension phase, evaluating safety and efficacy of upadacitinib versus adalimumab (ADA) up to week 260 (~ 5 years).

METHODS: Data on treatment-emergent adverse events and all primary and secondary endpoints were collected through week 260 for patients who received a placebo or ≥ 1 dose of UPA at either 15 mg (UPA15) or 30 mg (UPA30) daily, or ADA 40 mg every other week. For non-radiographic binary endpoints, both observed data and non-responder imputation methods were used, whereas for radiographic binary endpoints, the observed data method was used. For continuous endpoints, observed data and mixed-effects model repeated-measures analyses were employed.

RESULTS: A total of 1704 patients received at least one dose of study drug, with 983 (57.7%) completing 260 weeks of treatment. The safety profile of UPA through week 260 was consistent with data from weeks 104 and 152. UPA treatment was associated with higher rates of serious infections, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, creatine kinase elevation, and non-melanoma skin cancer compared with ADA treatment. The exposure-adjusted incidence rates for major adverse cardiovascular events (n/100 PY [95% CI]: UPA15, 0.4 [0.2, 0.8]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.3 [0.1, 0.7]) and venous thromboembolism (UPA15, 0.2 [0.0, 0.5]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.2 [0.0, 0.6]) were low and comparable across treatment groups. Efficacy improvements observed with UPA at weeks 56 and 104 were maintained through week 260 and were comparable to those achieved with ADA.

CONCLUSIONS: The safety profile of UPA over 5 years remained consistent with that observed at weeks 104 and 152, with no new signals identified.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT03104400.

We now report the long-term extension phase, evaluating safety and efficacy of upadacitinib versus adalimumab (ADA) up to week 260 (~ 5 years). METHODS: Data on treatment-emergent adverse events and all primary and secondary endpoints were collected through week 260 for patients who received a placebo or ≥ 1 dose of UPA at either 15 mg (UPA15) or 30 mg (UPA30) daily, or ADA 40 mg every other week.

title: Endovascular Management of Life-Threatening Hemoptysis in Rare Pulmonary Vascular Diseases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Massive hemoptysis in patients with complex pulmonary vascular disease is difficult to manage because surgery is frequently contraindicated, making endovascular therapy an important treatment option.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 3 patients with life-threatening hemoptysis caused by distinct rare etiologies: systemic-to-pulmonary collateral bleeding in Eisenmenger syndrome due to patent ductus arteriosus, complex collateral bleeding associated with left upper lobe aspergilloma, and post-tubercular collateral hemorrhage. Angiography-guided transcatheter embolization was individualized using particles, coils, and a vascular plug according to vascular anatomy. All patients achieved immediate hemostasis without major procedural complications, with sustained freedom from recurrent hemoptysis during 6-12 months of follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Successful bronchial artery embolization depends on meticulous angiographic evaluation and anatomy-driven device selection. This series demonstrates the versatility of endovascular techniques, including vascular plug implantation for high-flow bronchial collaterals in cases where conventional embolization is technically challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Individualized, anatomy-guided endovascular therapy provides a safe, effective, and organ-preserving treatment for life-threatening hemoptysis in complex pulmonary vascular disease. Careful procedural planning is essential for durable clinical success.

Angiography-guided transcatheter embolization was individualized using particles, coils, and a vascular plug according to vascular anatomy.

title: Risk-benefit profile of upper versus lower extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal insertion site for peripherally inserted central catheters in neonates remains uncertain. International guidelines differ in their recommendations regarding upper- versus lower-extremity placement, and existing systematic reviews are limited by small samples, narrow outcome coverage, or outdated evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 6, 2026, for studies comparing upper- versus lower-extremity placement in neonates. Primary outcomes were venous thromboembolism, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter tip malposition; secondary outcomes included phlebitis, catheter migration, catheter leakage, catheter occlusion, catheter breakage, total complications, dwell time, unplanned removal, pericardial or pleural effusion, sepsis, and all-cause mortality. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Crude estimates were pooled, sparse and heterogeneous adjusted estimates were summarised narratively, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: Twenty-one observational studies from 10 countries, involving 15,289 catheters, were included. For primary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; P = 0.017; low certainty) but higher risks of central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.95; P = 0.018; very low certainty) and catheter tip malposition (RR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.61-4.30; P < 0.001; very low certainty). For secondary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with lower phlebitis risk (RR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.94; P = 0.022; low certainty) but higher risks of catheter migration (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27-2.38; P < 0.001; low certainty), catheter leakage (RR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.35-3.73; P = 0.002; moderate certainty), and a marginally higher risk of unplanned removal (RR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.00-1.51; P = 0.048; very low certainty). A post hoc exploratory analysis suggested a possible higher risk of pericardial or pleural effusion (RR = 3.79, 95% CI 1.20-12.02; P = 0.024; very low certainty). No statistically significant between-site differences were observed for other secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Crude observational evidence suggested a potential bidirectional risk-benefit profile across catheter-related outcomes. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because non-randomised designs remain susceptible to residual confounding. The observed associations may inform risk-informed, individualised site selection but do not establish a universally preferred site. Prospective studies with standardised outcomes and adjusted analyses are needed.

International guidelines differ in their recommendations regarding upper- versus lower-extremity placement, and existing systematic reviews are limited by small samples, narrow outcome coverage, or outdated evidence. OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates.

title: Impact of portable point-of-care ultrasound on clinical decision-making and referrals in general practice: a cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in general practice, but evidence on its impact on clinical decision-making when performed with portable devices remains limited. Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

METHODS: Cross-sectional observational study conducted over 12 months in a primary care centre in Barcelona, Spain. Three general practitioners with accredited training performed POCUS examinations using portable devices in 108 patients. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥15 years requiring clinical ultrasound. Clinical management plans were documented before and after POCUS using same questionnaire. Changes in decision-making and referral patterns were analysed using McNemar's test. Reporting followed the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

RESULTS: POCUS changed clinical decision-making in 66.7% of cases. Intended referrals to secondary care decreased from 44.4% to 25.0% (absolute risk reduction 19.4%, 95% CI 8.4-30.5%, relative risk reduction 44%). Musculoskeletal examinations represented 73.1% of cases, with management modified in 63.3%. All seven patients with suspected deep vein thrombosis were managed without hospital referral. Referrals for conventional radiology ultrasound decreased from 32.4% to 12.0%, while GP-performed invasive procedures (infiltrations) increased from 0.9% to 18.5%.

CONCLUSION: Portable POCUS substantially influences clinical decision-making and reduces secondary care referrals in general practice. Further research is needed, especially longitudinal studies, to evaluate whether these changes translate into improved health outcomes for patients.

Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death.

RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

title: Clinical and economic impact of central venous catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatric intensive care units: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central venous catheter-associated and catheter-related bloodstream infections may increase mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs in critically ill children. This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible. The exposure will be catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infection, compared with patients from the same catheter-exposed source population who are infection-free at the relevant risk time. Mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs are co-primary outcomes. Multiple bibliographic databases, gray-literature sources, and study registries will be searched without date restrictions. Two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, assess risk of bias, and evaluate certainty. Meta-analysis will be performed when studies are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis will be used.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The review is expected to clarify the magnitude and methodological robustness of the clinical and economic consequences of these infections and identify priorities for future pediatric intensive care research.

This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible.

title: [Predictive value and threshold effect analysis of the novel systemic immune-inflammatory complex index for functional outcomes at 90 days after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between the baseline systemic immune-inflammatory complex index (SIICI) and the 90-day functional prognosis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing reperfusion therapy, as well as the threshold effect.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled. Patients were divided into good prognosis group [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 0-2] and a poor prognosis group (mRS score was 3-6) according to the 90-day score after onset. The clinical data and blood routine indicators within 24 hours after onset were collected, and SIICI and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Univariate Logistic regression analysis was performed to screen 90-day functional prognosis-related influencing factors in patients with AIS after reperfusion therapy. Multivariate Logistic regression with multi-gradient adjustment was used to determine whether SIICI was an independent risk factor for poor functional prognosis or not. The restricted cubic spline (RCS) model was applied to analyze the dose-response relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor functional prognosis, and piecewise linear regression model was used for threshold effect analysis. Subjects were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7 : 3 for constructing a prognostic prediction model based on SIICI and internal validation. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were plotted to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit of the model.

RESULTS: All 1 919 AIS patients were enrolled in the final analysis, including 1 176 cases (61.28%) in the good prognosis group and 743 cases (38.72%) in the poor prognosis group. Univariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age, history of atrial fibrillation, bridging therapy, endovascular thrombectomy, elevated baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, prolonged total length of hospital stay, increased white blood cell count, elevated neutrophil count, elevated monocyte count, increased SII and elevated SIICI were risk factors for poor 90-day functional prognosis of AIS patients, and the history of hyperlipidemia and elevated lymphocyte count were protective factors (all P<0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for gender, age, past medical history, Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification and baseline NIHSS score, SIICI remained an independent risk factor for poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients [odds ratio (OR)=1.008, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.001-1.014, P=0.022], whereas SII showed no statistical significance after adjustment (OR=1.010, 95%CI was 0.999-1.020, P=0.067), suggesting that SIICI possessed better stability of independent association than the traditional inflammatory index SII. The RCS model verified a significant non-linear relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients (P<0.001). The optimal inflection point value of SIICI determined by piecewise linear regression was 15.03. When SIICI<15.03, each one-unit increase in SIICI was associated with an 11% increased risk of poor functional prognosis (OR=1.112, 95%CI was 1.078-1.147, P<0.001). When SIICI≥15.03, no statistically significant correlation was observed between SIICI and poor functional prognosis (OR=1.005, 95%CI was 0.998-1.012, P=0.136). For the SIICI-based prognosis prediction model, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.656 (95%CI was 0.626-0.686) in the training set and 0.639 (95%CI was 0.593-0.686) in the validation set, indicating favorable prognostic discrimination ability. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test yielded P=0.064, suggesting good model calibration. DCA revealed that the model obtained significant clinical net benefit within the high-risk threshold range of 0-0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SIICI is independently correlated with the 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients after reperfusion therapy and shows a significant threshold effect. It exhibits superior predictive performance compared with the traditional inflammatory index SII. The prognostic prediction model constructed based on SIICI can assist clinicians in stratifying the risk of early functional prognosis in patients with AIS undergoing reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled.

title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making.

METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons.

RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss.

CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base.

HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of adalimumab levels and anti-adalimumab antibodies in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the association between longitudinal adalimumab concentrations, anti-adalimumab antibodies (AAA) levels, and clinical response in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).

METHODS: A prospective multi-center, observational cohort study of AS patients receiving adalimumab therapy was conducted. Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization. Adalimumab concentrations were measured using a validated sandwich immunoassay. Measurement of AAA levels was performed with a laboratory-developed immunoassay system integrating electrochemiluminescence technology with specific immunomagnetic separation, with result reported as signal-to-noise ratio (S/N).

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients receiving adalimumab monotherapy were included. The median follow-up period was 169 days, and 711 plasma samples were available for adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels measurements. Seven patients had pre-existing AAA, and 120 (90.2%) of the remaining 133 patients tested positive for AAA during follow-up. A total of 48 patients were excluded from the exposure-response relationship dataset owing to pre-existing AAA (n=7), lack of active disease (n=26), incomplete follow-up (n=8), and prolonged dosing intervals (n=7). Among the remaining 92 patients, a total of 58 (63%) achieved clinical response. Adalimumab concentrations were higher, and AAA levels were significantly lower, in responders compared with non-responders at multiple time points. Exposure-response relationship models also revealed a steady-state adalimumab concentration target of 5.1 μg/mL and a week-4 concentration target of 3.3 μg/mL, corresponding to an 80% probability of clinical response. Thirty-six of 92 patients (39.1%) exhibited AAA-S/N values exceeding the putative clinically meaningful threshold (AAA-S/N=10). Patients in the high-AAA group (AAA-S/N≥10) had lower drug levels (median: 1.5 μg/mL vs. 6.9 μg/mL, P<0.0001) and poorer response rates (38.8% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.0002), relative to those in the low-AAA group (AAA-S/N<10). Furthermore, patients who were week-4 AAA-positive exhibited a 1.8-fold increased risk of non-response (relative risk, 95% confidence interval, 1.1-2.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that longitudinal profiles of adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels show a strong association with clinical responses in this Chinese AS cohort, which may inform therapeutic drug monitoring-guided adalimumab treatment strategies that remain to be further validated.

Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models.

RESULTS: Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU1wk-BL.

CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.

The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.
